_comment: T92 — shared vectors pinning the metre parser, the primitive that feeds beatPhase's groups. ONE parser, THREE runtimes that must never silently disagree: Go app.ParseMeter (T86 core), TS meterGroups (T86 studio), Kotlin (A35). The parser is deliberately LENIENT: a malformed metre never throws, it is treated as UNSET, which the beat reads as 4/4. `groups: null` therefore means 'the parser must treat this metre as unset' — and each runtime asserts that in its OWN idiom, because they cannot express 'unset' the same way: Go ParseMeter returns (nil, false); TS meterGroups returns the 4/4 default [1,1,1,1] (it never returns null); Kotlin asserts whatever unset shape it picks. A non-null `groups` is the exact grouping EVERY runtime must return. Grouping rule: an additive numerator (a+b+..) is taken literally; compound (n%3==0 && n>3) → n/3 groups of 3; simple → n groups of 1. Bounds: 1..16 groups, each 1..32, sum ≤ 64, denominator in {1,2,4,8,16}. This file is the source of truth; the in-code tables mirror it. Note for A35: when Kotlin mirrors this into commonTest/resources, add the CI drift-guard in that same commit — Go and TS read this path directly, so there is nothing to diff yet.

cases._: T92: whitespace INSIDE an additive numerator — each part is trimmed
double + → an empty middle part (Go: parse-fail; TS: 0 < 1)
non-ASCII digits, COMPOUND — discriminating: a naive parse gives [3,3], strict gives unset [1,1,1,1]
T92: empty numerator — Go fails to parse '', TS gets 0 which is < 1; same unset answer by different paths
